topic: Implicit Differentiation: Untangling the Hidden Slopes
target_audience: First-year university calculus students or advanced high school students

sections.title: The Mystery of the Tangled Equation
lecture_lines: In explicit functions, y stands alone, like y = 3x+2.
Implicit equations mix x and y together, like a knot.
Consider a circle's equation: x^2 + y^2 = 25.
Finding the slope here isn't as straightforward as before.
How do we differentiate without isolating y first?
animations: Show titles 'Explicit' (#00FF00) and 'Implicit' (#FF00FF) at top.
Display 'y = 3x + 2' (#00FF00) and 'x^2 + y^2 = 25' (#FF00FF).
Plot the graph of y = sqrt(25 - x^2) as a green semi-circle (#00FF00).
Transform the semi-circle into a full yellow circle (#FFFF00) x^2 + y^2 = 25.

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: The Chain Rule 'Sidecar'
lecture_lines: Since y depends on x, we use the Chain Rule.
Differentiating x^3 gives 3x^2 simply.
But differentiating y^3 requires a "sidecar" term.
We get 3y^2 times the derivative of y, dy/dx.
Always attach dy/dx when differentiating terms with y.
animations: Display 'd/dx [y^3]' in white (#FFFFFF).
Show '3y^2' appearing, then attach '(dy/dx)' in orange (#FF8800).
Display 'd/dx [x^3] = 3x^2' below, highlighting no (dy/dx) needed.

sections.title: The Step-by-Step 'Untangling' Algorithm
lecture_lines: Step one: Differentiate both sides with respect to x.
For x^2 + y^2 = 25, we get 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0.
Step two: Collect all dy/dx terms on one side.
Step three: Factor out dy/dx and solve algebraically.
The result: dy/dx equals negative x divided by y.
animations: Write equation 'x^2 + y^2 = 25' in center (#FFFFFF).
Animate terms changing to '2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0' with '(dy/dx)' in #FF8800.
Rearrange and simplify to show 'dy/dx = -x/y' in cyan (#00FFFF).

sections.title: Visualizing the Slopes on a Curve
lecture_lines: Look at the circle at point (3, 4).
Our formula gives a slope of negative three-fourths.
Notice how the tangent line matches this visual tilt.
animations: Plot a yellow circle x^2 + y^2 = 25 (#FFFF00) with point (3, 4) in red (#FF0000).
Draw a green tangent line (#00FF00) passing through (3, 4).
Display text 'slope = -3/4' near the tangent line (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Complex Application: The Elliptical Space-Thrust
lecture_lines: For an ellipse, x^2 + 4y^2 = 16, the process holds.
Differentiating yields 2x plus 8y times dy/dx equals zero.
Solving for dy/dx gives negative x over 4y.
animations: Plot the blue ellipse x^2 + 4y^2 = 16 (#0000FF).
Display the derivative step '2x + 8y(dy/dx) = 0' below the equation.
Highlight '8y(dy/dx)' with a pulsing orange box (#FF8800).
Show the result 'dy/dx = -x / 4y' in cyan (#00FFFF).
Animate a dot moving along the ellipse with a dynamic tangent vector.

sections.title: Summary & The 'Golden Rule'
lecture_lines: Always treat y as a hidden function of x.
Remember, the derivative of any constant is always zero.
Follow the flow: Differentiate, then group, then solve.
animations: Show flow chart: 'Differentiate' -> 'Group' -> 'Solve' in white boxes.
Display 'The Golden Rule: Treat y as f(x)' in yellow (#FFFF00).
Animate 'd/dx [constant] = 0' with the 0 flashing in red (#FF0000).
